# OpenAI's Images 2.6 Adds Short Animated GIFs, Faster Images, and Steadier Edits

> **In short:** OpenAI says its Images 2.6 update is available in ChatGPT and Codex and in its API. The company says it generates images about 50% faster, can turn a prompt into a short looping GIF, and keeps characters, products, and brand details more consistent while you edit.

Have you ever asked an AI for a simple picture, then watched it change your dog's color or a logo's shape with every new request? OpenAI's latest image update is aimed at exactly that kind of frustration.

## What is new

OpenAI says Images 2.6 brings three main changes:

- **Faster images.** The company says it generates pictures about 50% faster than before.
- **Animated GIFs.** A GIF (a short animation that loops over and over, like a tiny cartoon) can now be made from a single prompt. A **prompt** is simply the instruction you type to the AI.
- **Steadier edits.** OpenAI says characters, products, and brand details should stay the same as you refine an image.

The company also says people now create images across ChatGPT, Codex, and its API at a very large scale, in the billions each week.

## Making GIFs from a prompt

OpenAI's examples show that you can describe motion, not just a still scene. Instead of "a cartoon cat," you might describe the cat waving, then pausing, then waving again, and ask for it as a loop.

OpenAI suggests a few everyday uses: reactions and memes for social media, a mascot that waves for a small business, or a quick storyboard that shows how a character moves before a real video is shot. You do not need a polished drawing to start. The company says even a rough sketch can become an expressive animated character.

## What developers get

If you build tools or apps, you use the **API** (a way for two programs to talk to each other). OpenAI says the API now includes two image models. One is aimed at speed, and the company says it can produce some images in just a few seconds at its lowest quality setting. The other is aimed at detailed work, with higher quality and better consistency across edits at medium or high quality settings.

The API also gains tools that already exist in ChatGPT:

- **Image markup**: drawing on a picture to point at the exact spot you want changed.
- **SVG export**: SVG is a file format for drawings that stay sharp at any size, which helps with websites, apps, and printing.
- **Complexity**: a new setting that controls how much planning the model does. OpenAI recommends lower settings for most quick edits and higher ones for scenes with many parts.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life**: If you like making cards, memes, or classroom visuals, you can ask for a short looping animation instead of a single still picture.
- **For your work**: If you manage social media or a small business, a mascot or product shot can be turned into a loop without a designer. Keep a short list of brand colors and logos so you can check each result.
- **If you're just getting started**: Begin with one simple idea and describe it in plain words. Then ask for one change at a time, so you can see what the AI keeps and what it changes.
- **If you already use it**: If you work through the API, OpenAI recommends low complexity for most edits and medium or high for busy scenes. Test both on the same request and compare the results.

OpenAI says Images 2.6 is available in ChatGPT and Codex across all subscription tiers, on desktop, mobile, and web. For current plan details, check OpenAI's official pricing page, since prices can change.

## Wrap-up

OpenAI says Images 2.6 makes images faster, adds short animated GIFs, and keeps details steadier across edits. The simplest next step is to open ChatGPT, describe one small animation you would enjoy making, and see how close the first result comes. Then request one small change and notice what stays the same.
